cases.title: Drop blamed on temporary destocking, but a major customer is also insourcing
reasons: Judgment criterion 'Why the price is low' is not fully met: The 35% price decline is driven by both temporary customer destocking AND the announced loss of the second-largest customer (15% of sales) to that customer's own in-house platform starting 2027. This customer transition is structural for Veritest's revenue, not temporary.

The business model is strong (75% recurring revenue, well above 50% threshold) and profitable (16% EBITDA margin), with no kill criteria triggered (2.0x leverage, no holder above 25%, no regulatory issues, all in the preferred immunoassay segment).

However, the permanent loss of a major customer to a competing in-house solution represents a structural business change rather than a cyclical destocking event or temporary product transition. Viability depends on management's ability to replace this revenue.
missing_facts: Will Veritest remain profitably above competitive thresholds after losing 15% of sales in 2027?
